newsitem.title: HONG KONG: AsiaSat to grow with Asian telephony.
newsitem.headline: AsiaSat to grow with Asian telephony.

text.p: Asia Satellite Telecommunications Holdings Ltd will see rapid growth in demand from video and telephony providers, including Internet providers, said a senior executive on Tuesday.
"We are noticing in Asia a tremendous growth in telephony which I think isn't evident to people who are watching satellite and look only at video growth," said chief executive officer Peter Jackson.

The company had seen rapid growth in demand from both video and telecommunications providers but telecoms and data transmission grew faster, accounting for 35 percent of capacity utilised in 1996 compared with 30 percent last year, said Jackson.
"We have just announced that we just signed a transponder with an Internet provider," said Jackson. "This is another exciting area."
"Satellite is ideally suited for point to multi-point distribution of information," he said. "It is far better than any terrestial switch network."
The company reported profit attributable to shareholders of HK$395 million, a 134 percent increase over the company's pro forma 1995 results.
"This reflects the fact that we had AsiaSat 2 on line and the fact that there is still considerable demand and we are seeing that growth come through," Jackson said.
AsiaSat 2 was launched in November 1995 and was operational in January 1996.
The company's results exceeded forecasts made at the time of its listing in June 1996.
Revenue grew to HK$823 million, 9.0 percent higher than forecast and net profit was 30 percent higher, said Jackson.
The large rise in revenue, up 152 percent, was due to a dramatic increase in utilisation.

"We moved to an 87 percent utilisation on AsiaSat 1, and to an 83 percent on AsiaSat 2," said Jackson. "AsiaSat 1 is in one of the most attractive spots in Asia, but AsiaSat 2 is a higher powered satellite with a larger footprint."
The company's two largest customers are News Corp's Star TV, which accounts for 39 percent of total revenue and the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television in China.
Revenue from Chinese customers accounted for 27 percent of total turnover.
Asia Satellite's prices were believed to be about 10 percent higher than its competitors, but its high quality transponders with a broader geographic reach made it a competitive choice, Jackson said.
Cable and Wireless Plc, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd and CITIC Pacific Ltd each hold a 23.00 percent stake in the company.
The share price of Asia Satellite closed HK$0.30 higher at HK$19.70 on Tuesday.
